steps.title: Import TypeScript types and utilities
steps.instruction: Import the Record utility type and create a NormalizedState interface from TypeScript's built-in types.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to import Record and 'interface' to define NormalizedState with generic types T and K.
steps.seedCode: // Import Record utility type and define NormalizedState interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the foundational TypeScript types needed for typed normalization of entities.
successCriteria: Record type is imported and NormalizedState interface is defined with byId and allIds properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported the Record utility type and defined the NormalizedState interface with proper generics.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to import Record and define the NormalizedState interface with both byId and allIds properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported the Record type and defined the NormalizedState interface with the correct structure.

steps.title: Define the Entity interface
steps.instruction: Create an Entity interface with an id property of type number and a name property of type string.
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword followed by the name Entity, then define the properties inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Record utility type and define NormalizedState interface here

// Create the Entity interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: An Entity interface is defined with the required typed properties.
successCriteria: The Entity interface exists with id: number and name: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a strongly-typed Entity interface, which will serve as the base structure for our normalized data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both id and name properties are included with the correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Entity interface wasn't defined correctly. Check that you used the interface keyword and included both required properties with proper types.

steps.title: Define the NormalizedState type
steps.instruction: Create a NormalizedState type with two properties: entities (a Record mapping string IDs to Entity objects) and ids (an array of strings).
steps.hint: Use the Record utility type from TypeScript for the entities property. The ids property should be an array of strings.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a NormalizedState type that defines the structure for storing normalized entity data.
successCriteria: The NormalizedState type is defined with entities (Record<string, Entity>) and ids (string[]) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the NormalizedState type with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure both properties (entities and ids) are included with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NormalizedState type definition is missing or incorrect. Check that it has both required properties with proper types.

steps.title: Create the initial normalization function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'normalizeEntities' that takes an array of Entity objects as a parameter and returns a NormalizedState object.
steps.hint: Define a function with the specified name, parameter type (Entity[]), and return type (NormalizedState). Inside, you'll need to implement the normalization logic in later steps.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'normalizeEntities' is defined with the correct TypeScript signature.
successCriteria: The function 'normalizeEntities' exists, accepts an Entity[] parameter, and returns NormalizedState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the normalization function with the proper TypeScript signature. This establishes the foundation for implementing the normalization logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the function name, parameter type, or return type. Make sure it matches 'normalizeEntities(entities: Entity[]): NormalizedState'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Create a function named 'normalizeEntities' that takes an array of Entity objects and returns a NormalizedState object.

steps.title: Add type parameters to the normalization function
steps.instruction: Make your normalization function generic by adding a type parameter <T extends Entity> to the function signature.
steps.hint: Add <T extends Entity> after the function name, then use T instead of Entity for the parameter and return types.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will accept any type that satisfies the Entity interface, providing better type safety.
successCriteria: The normalizeEntities function has a type parameter <T extends Entity> and uses T for both the parameter type and return type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully made the function generic, allowing it to work with any type that extends Entity while preserving type information.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've added the type parameter <T extends Entity> and updated both the parameter and return types to use T.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should be generic. Add <T extends Entity> after the function name and replace Entity with T in the parameter and return type annotations.

steps.title: Create a User entity interface
steps.instruction: Define a User interface that extends the Entity interface and adds an email property of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword, followed by 'User', then 'extends Entity', and finally declare the email property inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A User interface is created that extends Entity and includes an email property.
successCriteria: The User interface extends Entity and has an email property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the User interface with the required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the User interface extends Entity and includes an email property of type string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The User interface should extend Entity and include an email property of type string.

steps.title: Initialize sample user data
steps.instruction: Create an array of User objects with id, name, and email properties. Name the array 'sampleUsers'.
steps.hint: Define a constant array with at least two User objects, each having id (string), name (string), and email (string) properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a sampleUsers array containing User objects with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: The sampleUsers array is defined with at least two User objects, each containing id, name, and email properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created sample user data that matches the User interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an array, but make sure it contains User objects with id, name, and email properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sampleUsers array is missing or doesn't match the User interface requirements.

steps.title: Normalize the user data
steps.instruction: Call the normalizeEntities function with your sample user array and store the result in a constant named normalizedUsers.
steps.hint: Use the function you created earlier, passing the user array as the argument. Assign the result to a constant with type annotation.

steps.title: Create a denormalization function
steps.instruction: Create a function named denormalizeState that takes a NormalizedState<T> and returns an array of T entities.
steps.hint: The function should iterate through allIds and map each id to its corresponding entity in byId.
steps.expectedOutcome: A denormalizeState function that converts normalized state back to an array of entities.
successCriteria: The denormalizeState function is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns an array of entities.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the denormalization function that can restore the original array structure from normalized state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function accepts a NormalizedState<T> parameter and returns T[].
steps.feedbackWrong: The denormalization function isn't quite right. It should take normalized state and return an array of entities.

steps.title: Test the normalization round-trip
steps.instruction: Call the denormalization function with the normalized state to verify it reconstructs the original user array, then log both the original and reconstructed arrays to the console.
steps.hint: Use the denormalizeEntities function you created earlier, passing it the normalized state object. Store the result in a variable, then log both the original users array and the reconstructed array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The console will show that the original user array and the denormalized array are identical, confirming the normalization/denormalization process works correctly.
successCriteria: The denormalizeEntities function is called with the normalized state, the result is stored, and both original and reconstructed arrays are logged to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully verified that your normalization and denormalization functions work together correctly, showing that the typed entity normalization preserves data integrity.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling denormalizeEntities with the normalized state you created earlier, storing the result, and logging both the original users array and the reconstructed array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to call the denormalizeEntities function with your normalized state, store the result, then log both the original users array and the reconstructed array to verify they match.
